scientific_scope: Synthetic ranking-and-selection method evaluation only; no OpenMC transport, reactor physics validation, benchmark acceptance, fuel-management recommendation, or safety claim.
primary_endpoint: Fraction of independent candidate pools in which the selected candidate satisfies the predeclared latent synthetic feasibility rule.
confirmatory_unit: candidate pool; methods compared pairwise on the exact same pool and same candidate observations

development.purpose: Choose uniform-margin baseline only; do not pool development results into confirmatory estimates.
development.selection_rule: Maximize development-pool latent feasible-selection rate; break ties in favor of the smallest margin.

confirmation.candidate_pool_draw: sample 12 distinct feasible candidates from the 7-position toy QUBO candidate space; each method receives the same candidate set and the same noisy observations

synthetic_truth.heteroscedastic_rule: sigma is low when arrangement_indicator is 0 and high when it is 1
synthetic_truth.arrangement_indicator: sum of one-based positions with fresh label, modulo 2
synthetic_truth.note: The latent response generator is artificial and intentionally labeled synthetic; it is not a physical model.

fixed_method_parameters.QUBO_method: lowest QUBO energy in the same candidate pool
fixed_method_parameters.uniform_margin: chosen on 200 development pools only and frozen before confirmatory scoring

statistics.confidence_interval: paired pool-level percentile bootstrap, 5000 resamples, deterministic bootstrap seed
statistics.superiority_gate: demonstrate synthetic superiority only if the paired 95% interval lower bound is greater than zero against both point-estimate and development-tuned uniform-margin baseline in each of the three calibrated Gaussian regimes; stress regimes are reported separately and cannot rescue a failed primary gate
statistics.stress_interpretation: No-feasible and misspecified-noise results are robustness diagnostics, not part of the superiority gate.

explicit_nonclaims: Not OpenMC or C5G7 physical validation.
Not evidence of reactor safety or fuel-management benefit.
Not quantum hardware execution or quantum advantage.
A favorable synthetic result does not validate the uncertainty model used on physical simulations.
